question: A list screen sorts courses by title only. Several courses share the title "Java". Users report that one of them shows up on both page 1 and page 2. What is the fix?
options: Increase the page size
Add a unique tiebreaker, so the sort is title and then id
Switch the return type from Page to List
Sort in Java after loading the page
explanation: Rows with equal titles have no defined relative order, so it can differ between two queries. Ending the sort with the id gives every row one fixed position.

question: A mobile feed shows a "Load more" button and never displays the total number of items. Which return type avoids unneeded work?
options: Page, because it is the default
List without a Pageable
Optional
Slice, because it knows if a next slice exists without a COUNT query
explanation: Slice fetches one extra row to detect a next slice and runs no count. Page would execute a COUNT on every request for a number nobody sees.

question: An endpoint declares a Pageable parameter. A client calls it with `?size=100000&sort=salary`. Salary is not part of the public API. What should the service do?
options: Cap the size and reject sort properties that are not on a whitelist
Trust the values, because Spring validated them
Ignore the size and return everything
Convert the sort to uppercase
explanation: Spring binds page and sort values without checking them against your public contract. The application enforces a maximum size and the allowed sort fields.

question: A log export pages through 40 million events with page and size parameters. Page 20,000 takes seconds while page 1 takes milliseconds. Which change addresses the cause?
options: Use keyset pagination so each request starts after the last seen key
Make the page size smaller
Add EAGER fetching
Switch from Page to Slice only
explanation: With an offset the database must read and discard all earlier rows. A keyset condition on indexed sort columns jumps straight to the next rows.

question: A controller returns `Page<CourseSummary>` straight from the repository and a client app parses its JSON. Why is that risky?
options: Page cannot be serialized at all
The JSON contains the SQL that ran
The implementation class is a framework type whose JSON can change, so a custom response record or PagedModel is a safer contract
Clients cannot read arrays
explanation: The Spring Data reference advises against exposing PageImpl directly because its representation is not a stable API. Your own record fixes the contract.
